question.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡z$ that passes through the point $P(4,3,e).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4,3,e) & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡e=\sqrt{25}-1=4\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=4.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡z & =4 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡z \\ {e}^{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4} & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z} \\ {e}^{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4} & =z\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(4,3,e)$ is the surface $z={e}^{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4}.$
